$description: Navigator › Data: every state entry this document defines, grouped by what KIND of thing it is, and — under the one you opened — the fields that define it beside the value it resolved to. `panels/signals-panel.ts` keeps every decision: what category an entry falls in, what its badge and its one-line summary say, which of nine controls each field of a `$prototype` gets, what a commit is worth, what a rename collides with, and which four surfaces are islands rather than fields. This document draws the answer. Two things follow from that split and are worth stating. THE FIELD LIST IS A PROJECTION, not a shape per category: a `Request` and an `IndexedDB` entry differ only in the rows the flow hands over, so adding a prototype is a case in TypeScript and no markup at all. And EVERY CONTROL HANDS BACK THE NAMES THAT PLACE IT — the entry, the field, and for a table cell its row and column — because the maps nest four deep and inside the innermost one `$map/item` is the cell: a control genuinely cannot see the entry it belongs to, and a name it can hand straight back is the whole answer.

style.$description: The `.signal-*`, `.signals-*` and `.data-*` rules of `styles/inspector.css`, carried here and keyed on `part`. A signal row is `part="entry"` rather than `part="row"` because the value tree mounted INSIDE an open one is `surfaces/panel-data.json`, whose lines are `part="row"`; two documents sharing a container may not share a part name. Three token repairs travel with them, all of the shape `surfaces/git-panel.json` describes: `--spectrum-font-size-50` and the bare `10px` literals resolved only inside `<sp-theme>` and a document is mounted outside it, so every rule that read one would silently have taken its px fallback — they are `--jx-text-sm` (11px) and `--jx-text-xs` (10px) here, at the same values — and `--spectrum-corner-radius-75` is `--jx-radius-xs`, also at its own value. ONE rule is repaired rather than moved: `.signal-badge.handler` never matched anything, because `defCategory` has returned `"function"` since the handler category was renamed, so a function entry's badge was the only one of five drawn untinted. The tint is keyed on the category the projection actually emits now, and `--handler` is the token it was always written against. And one is DELETED, because the kit already draws it: `.signal-del`'s hand-rolled visibility hiding is `[part="delete"]`'s reveal on `:hover` and on `:focus-within` — the old rule was `:hover` alone, so tabbing to Delete moved the keyboard onto an invisible control.

& [part=\"category\"].$description: The accordion header reads at the panel's own size rather than the kit's default, which is what `--spectrum-accordion-item-header-font-size` was set for.

& [part=\"disclosure\"].$description: A button dressed as the row it fills: no chrome of its own, the row's own cursor, and the three spans laid out exactly as the old div laid them out.

& [part=\"name\"].$description: The NAME is what you came for, so it is the last thing to be elided. It used to sit at `flex: 1` beside a hint pinned at `flex-shrink: 0`, so a long-prototype row rendered as `re… ContentCollect…` — the summary intact and the identity gone.

& [part=\"summary\"][data-tone=\"pending.$description: PENDING IS A RESTING STATE, not progress. While you are editing, an automatic `Request` is deliberately not fetched — so a value that has not arrived is dim and STILL, and the pulse below is kept for the one moment something is actually in flight. An animation that never stops is a spinner for a thing that is not loading, and it is why `probe.idle()` could not call this panel quiet.

& [part=\"field\"].$description: The editor's rows are narrower than the Inspector's: 65px of label at 10px, which is what `.signal-editor .field-row sp-field-label` set and what keeps a 240px Navigator readable.

& [part=\"cell-text\"].$description: A column's share of the row travels as a custom property under its own name, so a three-column row interns one rule instead of three inline `flex:` attributes.

@(forced-colors: active).$description: Every badge tint collapses into the page in forced colours, so the badge keeps a border of its own and the expanded row is marked by its rule rather than by a wash.

$props.label: Refresh
$props.hint: Re-run automatic fetches and read the canvas again

children.$description: Absent entirely until there is something to refresh: the verb re-runs automatic `Request` entries, and a project with no state entries has none. `loading` is the kit's own spinner swap, so the panel does not carry a second one.

The disclosure is the BUTTON and the row is the box around it, rather than the row being a `role="button"` with a second button inside it: a delete nested in a control is a control the keyboard reaches by leaving the one it is in. The badge, the name and the summary are what the button is made of, so its accessible name is the entry and what the entry became.

code.$description: A function body written as source, which is a control that owns its row: the `bar` above it already says `Body` and holds the mode switch, so a labelled field here would print the word twice. Committed as it is typed, exactly as the textarea it replaces was.

hint.$description: A sentence about the whole entry rather than about one field of it — the class an imported prototype resolves to, what a plugin schema says it is for, or that the schema has not arrived yet. No label, because there is no value beside it to name.

true.$description: §7.1's inline tier: why the value is refused, said AT the control that refuses it and for as long as the value stays bad. The rename collision this exists for used to be a silent no-op — the field kept the typed name, the document kept the old one, and only the canvas could tell you which had won.

text.$description: Label plus one line. `jx-field` owns the label, the invalid shade and the association between the two, which is the whole of what `ui/field-row.ts`'s `.style-row` carried.

slot-field.$description: A labelled row whose control belongs to another surface — the media picker. The document renders the host and nothing in it (studio-ui-guidelines.md §9.4).

slot.$description: A full-width island: the expression editor, the statement-card editor, or the shared schema form. Each is a surface of its own that three other places embed, so this document renders an empty host and `panels/signals-panel.ts` fills it.

bar.$description: A heading with the controls that act on the whole of what is under it: the Body mode switch, and the button that opens the same value in the Bottom dock. The segments are a projection — the flow says which one is on — so nothing here knows that an array body is `Statements`.

children.$description: The basic parameter editor: one chip per name, and a field that mints another. Enter commits, because the chip IS the commit — there is nothing else in the row to leave.

true.$description: The basic/advanced switch, drawn as the quiet text link it has always been rather than as a second control: it changes how much of ONE value is on screen, not what the value is.

children.$description: What this entry BECAME, under the fields that define it. The border above it is the seam between the two halves that used to be two panels (plan §11.2).

empty.$description: Drawn here rather than borrowed from `panels/empty-state.ts`, which is a lit template a document cannot call. What is kept is the pattern's rules (§11): one sentence saying what the region is for, then the action that fills it.

children.$description: One picker, and its rows are GROUPED rather than divided: `jx-select` draws both halves of a group's delimiter, so "Data sources" and "Project imports" are named instead of being three unlabelled rules the reader has to infer. Picking a row is the whole gesture — the flow mints a free name, seeds the template and opens the entry — so the control never rests on what was picked, and `addSignal` announces the pick and then the empty string so the binding has a change to write back.
